title: Level 4 (Expert) - C-13
notes:
West leads the ♥5 against 4♠. East wins the ♥A and returns the suit, West ruffing. West's club return is won by South.

South is left with 2 possible losers in diamonds, but there are elimination possibilities. South should draw a round of trump in the closed hand, noting that East began with a singleton spade. The other top club honour is cashed and a spade is played to dummy's ♠A. Dummy's last club is ruffed, eliminating that suit.

When East follows to 3 rounds of clubs, South must hope East began with 1813 distribution with a singleton honour in diamonds. South exits with a low diamond. If West ducks, East will win the trick and be forced to lead a heart, conceding a ruff and discard. If West wins the trick, he will be endplayed. A diamond return allows South to lose only 1 diamond trick by playing the ♦10. A club return concedes a ruff and discard.

If East counts out to 2 diamonds, South must hope his doubleton contains 2 honours. In this case, South must cash the ♦A before exiting a small diamond. West must duck or dummy's ♦10 will be built into a trick. East will win and be endplayed as before.
